_**Boat Songs**_ is the third solo album by American musician [MJ Lenderman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MJ_Lenderman "MJ Lenderman"). It was released on April 29, 2022, by Dear Life Records.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boat_Songs#cite_note-Bandcamp-3) The album was listed on several publications' lists of the best albums of 2022.

## Release

\[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Boat_Songs&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Release")\]

On January 25, 2022, [Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum") managing editor Chris DeVille announced the release date of the album alongside the music video for "Hangover Game," comparing the album to [Jason Molina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Molina "Jason Molina"), [Uncle Tupelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncle_Tupelo "Uncle Tupelo"), and [Pinegrove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinegrove_(band) "Pinegrove (band)").[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boat_Songs#cite_note-4) In March, Stereogum senior editor Tom Breihan posted the music video for second single "TLC Cage Match." The song is named after the [tables, ladders, and chairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tables,_ladders,_and_chairs "Tables, ladders, and chairs") WWE match style, which it uses as a metaphor for self-destructive behavior.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boat_Songs#cite_note-5)

On April 29, 2022, _Boat Songs_ was released on Dear Life Records via Bandcamp in digital form, CD, vinyl, and cassette.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boat_Songs#cite_note-Bandcamp-3)

## Critical reception

\[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Boat_Songs&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

| Review scores |
| --- |
| Source | Rating |
| _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_(website) "Pitchfork (website)")_ | 8.3/10[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boat_Songs#cite_note-Pitchfork-6) |
| _[Uncut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncut_(magazine) "Uncut (magazine)")_ | ![Star](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Star_full.svg/20px-Star_full.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)![Star](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Star_full.svg/20px-Star_full.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)![Star](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Star_full.svg/20px-Star_full.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)![Star](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Star_full.svg/20px-Star_full.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Star_empty.svg/20px-Star_empty.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boat_Songs#cite_note-Uncut-7) |

Professional ratings

Sasha Geffen at _[Pitchfork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitchfork_(website) "Pitchfork (website)")_ praised Lenderman's [alt-country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_country "Alternative country") songwriting for its "disarming insights into the fray of living" delivered with fuzzy, lo-fi distortion, "loping, lackadaisical melodic phrasing," and "gentle, unhurried deadpan."[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boat_Songs#cite_note-Pitchfork-6) Dillon Riley, writing for _[Flood Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flood_Magazine "Flood Magazine")_, characterized Lenderman's writing as economical, yet low-brow compared to the more literary writing of his [Wednesday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wednesday_(American_band) "Wednesday (American band)") bandmate Karly Hartzman.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boat_Songs#cite_note-8) _[Uncut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncut_(magazine) "Uncut (magazine)")'_ s Erin Osmon described _Boat Songs_ with comparisons to [John Prine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Prine "John Prine"), [Neil Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Young "Neil Young") and [Crazy Horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crazy_Horse_(band) "Crazy Horse (band)"), and [Drive-By Truckers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drive-By_Truckers "Drive-By Truckers")'s [Patterson Hood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patterson_Hood "Patterson Hood"), praising Lenderman's "refreshing and thoroughly unpretentious perspective" that, by imbuing working-class signifiers with depth and importance, blurs the boundary between high and low art.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boat_Songs#cite_note-Uncut-7)
